faq.a: Dewi is associated with the Sanskrit form دِيوِي, whose core sense is dewi; goddess (sanskrit).

faq.q: What is the origin of Dewi?
faq.a: Dewi is associated with Sanskrit. Dewi is the Indonesian form of Sanskrit देवी (devī), meaning 'goddess'. It is used as a female given name.
No — the underlying form is Sanskrit, not Arabic.
Dewi can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Sanskrit-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Dewi should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Devī is a Sanskrit word, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Dewi mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Dewi is rendered دیوی and carries the sense دیوی، دیوی.

faq.q: What does Dewi mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Dewi is rendered دیوی and carries the sense دیوی، ایزدبانو.
A romanized syllable approximation is de-wi. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Dewi?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Dewi, dewi. Script forms are ديوي, دِيوِي, دیوی, देवी.

faq.q: Is Dewi a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
